headline: Hollywood is bending the knee to OpenAI
summary: Major studios like Amazon, Netflix, and Warner Bros. have reportedly passed on distributing 'Artificial,' a film about OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, following significant investments in AI.
details: Netflix, A24, Focus Features, and Warner Bros.' Clockwork have reportedly passed on Luca Guadagnino's "Artificial," a biographical drama about OpenAI cofounder Sam Altman. This reluctance signals a potential shift in Hollywood's willingness to tell critical stories about Big Tech.

Amazon MGM unexpectedly dropped "Artificial" last week, despite post-production being nearly finished and initial plans for an Oscar-qualifying theatrical run. Wider release plans for 2027 and a SXSW showing are now also canceled.

While Amazon cited the film being "better served by a different studio," this decision follows its $50 billion investment in OpenAI earlier this year. The company's push into AI likely influenced its reluctance to release a potentially negative portrayal of an AI executive.

Written by Simon Rich, "Artificial" chronicles Altman's tumultuous 2023 period, when he was fired from OpenAI and then rehired days later. The drama involved allegations of Altman not being "consistently candid" and hundreds of employees threatening to quit.

This trend extends beyond Amazon; A24 recently announced a $75 million "research partnership" with Google's DeepMind AI arm. This deal, aimed at developing filmmaking technologies, has drawn significant online criticism for A24.

headline: LastPass notifies users of yet another data breach, this time via an outside partner
summary: LastPass users are being warned about stolen personal data, with the latest incident stemming from one of the company's external partners.
details: LastPass users have once again received notifications regarding stolen personal data. This latest breach reportedly occurred through one of the company's outside partners, marking another security incident for the password manager.

The notification indicates that sensitive user information may have been compromised. While the exact scope and nature of the stolen data are still being assessed, users are advised to remain vigilant.
This incident follows a series of past security events involving LastPass, raising further concerns about the protection of user credentials and personal information stored within the service.
